yt.title: IPv6 gives every square millimeter of Earth {c_stat} addresses #Shorts
yt.description:
IPv6 has 2^128 = {c_tot} addresses. Earth surface area about 510.1 million km2. Divided evenly: {c_stat} addresses per square millimeter.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.narration: IPv6 will not run out of addresses. Here is how big it really is.

scenes.label: addresses per square millimeter of Earth
scenes.narration: IPv6 has two to the one hundred twenty eight addresses. Spread over the whole surface of the Earth, that is about {c_r_say} times ten to the {c_r_exp_say} for every square millimeter.
IPv4 had only about four point three billion. That is why it ran out.
